title: POC Weekly: Latency Tuning - Aurora Bank
summary: Weekly POC sync for latency tuning. Reviewed TTFT improvements with streaming enabled, sequence length tradeoffs, kernel selection on p4d vs A100, and KV cache sizing. Agreed to run a 2-week burst test on Dedicated with quantized model variant and streaming enabled; Redwood to share updated benchmark sheet and security appendix.
topics: kernel choices / GPU types (p4d vs A100)
KV cache sizing and prefix caching
action_items: Jordan Lee - share updated benchmark spreadsheet with 99th/median latencies and TTFT breakdown by audio/text payload - due 2026-09-17
Priya Nair - run kernel comparison between p4d and A100 for 2048 and 4096 seq lengths, include CPU fallback numbers - due 2026-09-22
Devon Shaw - provide production-like request distribution and percentiles (p95/p99) for two busiest endpoints - due 2026-09-18
Sofia Ramos - confirm required retention for audit logs and KMS key rotation window, send to Jordan - due 2026-09-20

transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-09-15
Time: 16:00 UTC
Duration: ~50 minutes
Attendees: Jordan Lee (Redwood AE), Priya Nair (Redwood SE), Sam Ortega (Redwood SE), Mark Hernandez (Aurora VP Eng), Lina Park (Aurora Platform), Devon Shaw (Aurora SRE), Sofia Ramos (Aurora Security)

Summary (auto-gen, may be imperfect): Reviewed latency numbers from last week's tests; streaming enabled shows lower TTFT for short responses but adds complexity to client; kernel mismatch observed on p4d causing higher variance at 4096 seq; KV cache sizing needs bump; security asks around KMS and audit retention noted.

[00:00] Jordan: hey everyone thanks for joining, uh we've got about 50 minutes on the calendar, quick roll call please
[00:08] Mark: Mark here, Lina, Devon, Sofia all on my side
[00:12] Lina: hi all
[00:14] Devon: yep
[00:16] Jordan: great, Priya and Sam from the tech team here, quick agenda  recap last week's TTFT numbers, dig into streaming behavior and sequence lengths, kernel choices on p4d vs a100, then security/next steps
[00:28] Priya: quick note, we pushed a minor config change yesterday that enables streaming by default on the test cluster - that will affect the TTFT numbers in the sheet Jordan shared
[00:36] Lina: we saw that, and a few of our clients noticed partial responses; some SDKs had to handle chunk reassembly differently
[00:44] Jordan: yeah that was expected, streaming improves first-token time but depends on client buffering, so we want to compare both flows
[00:52] Sam: noted a mislabel in the last benchmark file - the 95th numbers were actually medians, so updated sheet coming
[00:58] Mark: okay that's important, p99 and TTFT are what our SLAs measure
[01:05] Priya: jumping into the numbers  so with streaming enabled on p4d, TTFT median went from ~180ms to ~80ms for short replies (<=64 tokens). Median token latency improves but the variance widened at p99 when sequence length spikes
[01:25] Devon: can you unpack variance? is that warmup, GC, or kernel scheduling?
[01:29] Priya: looks like kernel scheduling across multi-instance GPUs  when we schedule mixed seq lengths the attention kernel selection sometimes chooses a fallback path that is less optimal; on A100 it's more consistent because of different kernel set. We saw a couple of outliers at 4096 where the kernel couldn't use the fused attention path and fell back
[01:48] Jordan: to translate - streaming gives you lower TTFT for small messages but if you have occasional long sequences your p99 can degrade unless we pin kernels or use a model variant tuned for long context
[01:59] Mark: our workload is mostly short alerts but we do have rare long transcripts (call recordings) that come in off-hours, those are bursty and cause the spikes
[02:12] Priya: makes sense  we recommend either segregating long-seq requests into a different route or using a quantized long-context variant for those; also KV cache prefixing helps a lot for repeated context
[02:26] Lina: what's KV cache sizing impact? Devon has been hitting OOMs in the test cluster when we tried caching everything
[02:34] Devon: yeah the KV seems to grow quickly with multiple concurrent users, OOM on a single worker happened twice yesterday
[02:40] Sam: we think the default cache retention is too high for your distribution; reducing retention and using prefix-only cache for common prompts will reduce memory footprint and preserve latency gains
[02:52] Priya: also worth noting, streaming reduces memory pressure on the client side but not necessarily server-side if full KV per request retained; we can tune TTLs and implement a per-route cache cap
[03:05] Jordan: on kernel choices  we ran both p4d and A100 during last burst. p4d had slightly better median but worse p99 at long seqs due to a missing fused kernel path for that model/quantization combination
[03:20] Mark: when you say fused kernel, you mean the attention+softmax fused op?
[03:24] Priya: yes, exactly - fused attention + rotary optimizations; some kernels are only available in our runtime on A100 tensor core stacks, p4d has different tuning and occasionally falls back to generic CUDA kernels
[03:38] Lina: so what's the practical recommendation for us  dedicated A100 or p4d? cost is a factor but SLAs matter
[03:46] Jordan: financial tradeoffs aside  if consistent p99 is critical, A100 Dedicated with pinned kernel profile and a long-context variant is safer. If you want better median at lower cost, p4d with aggressive batching and streaming might work but you'd need segregation for long contexts
[04:05] Mark: can Redwood do a split-route test where short requests hit streaming p4d pool and long ones go to A100? We could route by estimated seq length client-side
[04:15] Priya: yes, smart routing supports that  we can configure by-length thresholds and fallback rules. We'll need your production distribution to set thresholds properly
[04:25] Devon: we'll provide a histogram of sequence lengths and percentiles  should that include tokenization differences? we use a custom tokenizer on some data
[04:33] Sam: please include both raw character lengths and post-tokenization counts  tokenization affects kernel selection and batching effectiveness
[04:41] Mark: about TTFT  we need to define measurement. Is TTFT just time-to-first-token at server, or end-to-end including network + client processing?
[04:50] Priya: good question; our TTFT numbers are server-side (time from request arrival to first byte emitted). For SLA you might want end-to-end measured from the client perspective. We can instrument a synthetic client to measure e2e
[05:02] Jordan: we'll add e2e numbers to the spreadsheet as a separate column when we share the updated benchmarks
[05:08] Sofia: quick security item  if we burst to Dedicated, we need to ensure KMS integration and key rotation windows align with our policy, also audit log retention at 7 years is a ask from compliance
[05:18] Jordan: noted, we have an enterprise security appendix; some fields were redacted last time  I'll share the full appendix and we can book a security-only call next week
[05:26] Lina: also SSO/SAML mapping  we noticed some role mapping gaps in the dev console when trying to test RBAC
[05:33] Sam: that's on us, we'll sync with your identity admin and iterate on the SAML attribute mappings; shouldn't block the POC tests though
[05:40] Mark: good, next the bench results  Jordan, can you walk us through the updated sheet you prepared?
[05:46] Jordan: sure  linking the live sheet here: https://redwood.ai/poc-benchmarks/aurora-2026-09-15 (note: internal link)
[05:54] Jordan: column A is workload id, B is route (short vs long), C median TTFT, D p95, E p99, F e2e-simulated, G model variant, H GPU type, I streaming on/off
[06:08] Priya: example row  short-route, streaming ON, 64-token median TTFT ~78ms on p4d, p99 ~320ms; on A100 median ~95ms but p99 ~180ms for same workload
[06:24] Devon: long-route numbers?
[06:26] Priya: long-route 4096 tokens, streaming off, A100 median ~1.1s p99 ~1.6s; p4d median ~1.0s but p99 jumps to ~2.8s due to kernel fallback
[06:38] Mark: so despite better median on p4d for long, p99 is worse  that matches what we saw in production spikes
[06:44] Jordan: correct, and those p99 outliers align with the times where the runtime selected a non-fused attention kernel during concurrent requests
[06:53] Lina: is there a mitigation other than isolating the long requests? like forcing a kernel selection or changing model compilation flags?
[06:59] Priya: we can pin a kernel profile for a route  effectively telling the runtime to prefer fused kernels and reject incompatible quantized variants. That can increase latency for some tokens but stabilizes p99
[07:12] Sam: compilation step: we can rebuild the kernel set for p4d to include more fused paths but it's non-trivial and may require different CUDA toolchain; A100 already has the optimized kernels in our standard stack
[07:24] Mark: for the POC what's the least risky path?
[07:27] Jordan: provision A100 Dedicated for the 2-week burst and run a side-by-side with p4d streaming for short route. We'll capture e2e and server TTFT, and run percentiles under realistic traffic from your histograms
[07:38] Mark: ok do it  cost approvals are in place for the burst test but we'll need a clear expiry date
[07:44] Jordan: we'll set the burst for 7 days initially, extendable to 14 pending results; Redwood will absorb initial setup and share detailed cost projection for the burst window
[07:55] Sofia: security condition  no keys stored in plaintext on instances, KMS-only; and we need audit logs accessible via S3 with lifecycle policies
[08:03] Jordan: absolutely, KMS only, HSM-backed if required; audit logs to S3 with access controls. I'll attach the appendix with the ingestion pipeline diagram
[08:12] Devon: one more perf note  when we tried streaming in our SDK some clients needed to increase receive buffer timeouts, otherwise partials were dropped by the client stack
[08:22] Priya: yep, client timeouts need to be tuned; streaming trades off immediate first-byte for incremental delivery complexity on client. We can provide SDK patches for chunk reassembly
[08:32] Lina: can you include those SDK patches in the repo? we want to test before the burst goes live
[08:36] Sam: yes, will push a PR to your private repo with sample client changes by Friday
[08:42] Mark: great. any blockers for starting the burst next week?
[08:46] Jordan: main blockers: getting your real request distribution by EOD Friday, security acceptance on KMS/audit retention, and SAML role mapping confirmation. If those are green we can schedule provisioning Monday
[08:58] Mark: we'll aim for that; Devon will send the distribution and Sofia will review the security appendix
[09:04] Priya: quick follow-up on quantization  we tested 4-bit quantized variant and saw similar median but slightly worse p99 on p4d; on A100 quantized variant was stable. So quantization interacts with kernel availability too
[09:18] Jordan: final recap: Jordan to share updated benchmark spreadsheet and security appendix (includes KMS/audit/LZ configs); Priya to run kernel comparisons and share logs; Sam to PR client SDK patches; Aurora to share histograms and confirm SAML mappings. Plan: provision Dedicated A100 burst, run 7d test comparing short-route streaming p4d vs A100 long-route.
[09:40] Mark: thanks everyone, schedule follow-up security meeting next week
[09:44] Jordan: thanks all  we'll send calendar invites and the sheet after this call
[09:49] Lina: thanks folks
[09:50] (meeting ends)

Notes: transcription contains minor inaccuracies; speaker overlaps and automatic captions may have substituted some product names (e.g., "K-V cash" for KV cache, "fused kernel" sometimes transcribed as "fuse kernel").
